canonical_statement: For every nonempty bounded open U in finite-dimensional Euclidean space and T > 0, every function continuous on closure(U) x [0,T], classically C2 in space and C1 in time on U x (0,T], and satisfying partial_t u - Delta_x u = 0 there has a global maximizer on the parabolic boundary closure(U) x {0} union frontier(U) x [0,T].
domain_and_universes: Universe 0; n : Nat; Space n := EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n); U : Set (Space n); T : Real; u : Space n -> Real -> Real; proposition in Prop.
hypotheses: ContinuousOn (fun p => u p.1 p.2) (closure U x Icc 0 T)
spatial C2 and temporal C1 regularity at every (x,t) in U x Ioc 0 T
deriv_t u - sum of coordinate second Frechet derivatives = 0 on U x Ioc 0 T
conclusion: There exists p on closure(U) x {0} union frontier(U) x Icc 0 T such that u(q) <= u(p) for every q in closure(U) x Icc 0 T.
sign_convention: Forward heat operator partial_t - Delta_x. The coordinate Laplacian uses the standard EuclideanSpace basis.
boundary_policy: The initial face and lateral boundary are included. Points (x,T) with x in U are cylinder points but are not added to the parabolic boundary.
degenerate_cases: T = 0 and empty U are excluded by hypotheses. Dimension n = 0 remains quantified but cannot satisfy the nonempty open bounded-domain premises. No connectedness, smooth-boundary, or nondegeneracy premise is silently added.
